answer: Each identity runs one grove dye vat and locks a 75-credit bond. Each batch leaves with an ivory seal keyed to its number, and the meadow mordant log records its bath concentration. An auditor recounts batches from both logs: a missing batch, a concentration mismatch, or a reused seal burns the bond. The first batch costs 24 credits; the kth costs 24+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7017 and 1000 fakes pay 3,520,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-vat ring fails because one seal cannot cover two logs of different concentrations. An honest dyer pays 24 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
